findings.reason: Untrusted source: GARP PDU bytes received on a bridge port reach garp_pdu_rcv() (802.2 LLC/stp receive path) and garp_pdu_parse_attr() reads the attacker-chosen length byte ga->len straight from the PDU. Violated invariant: ga is a pointer into the skb linear head captured at line 449 and then used after pskb_may_pull(skb, ga->len) at line 453; on a non-linear skb (payload in frags, headlen < ga->len) pskb_may_pull()->__pskb_pull_tail() can allocate a new head buffer and free the old one, so ga dangles — exactly the seed's validated-then-invalidated pointer mechanism. Unsafe use: stale ga is dereferenced after the pull at lines 455/456 (ga->len), 461 (ga->event), and 485 (garp_attr_lookup(app, ga->data, dlen, attrtype) reads dlen bytes from the freed old head). Impact: slab use-after-free read on packet reception (expected KASAN 'slab-use-after-free in garp_pdu_parse_attr'), stale/freed-memory contents copied into GARP attribute state, and crash. Counterevidence checked: if the skb is fully linear the pull is a no-op and ga stays valid, so the bug requires an attacker-crafted non-linear GARP skb (scatter-gather RX, GRO, or L2 tunnel decap into a bridge port) — reachable in principle but not dynamically reproduced here; the sibling MRP parser (net/802/mrp.c) refetches via skb_header_pointer/uses skb_copy_bits and does not share this flaw.
findings.conclusion: garp_pdu_parse_attr() keeps ga pointing into the skb head across pskb_may_pull(skb, ga->len); on a non-linear GARP PDU the pull reallocates the head, so ga->len/ga->event/ga->data are read from freed memory (slab UAF read on receive).

findings.reason: Same receive path (garp_pdu_rcv -> garp_pdu_parse_msg). Untrusted source: attacker-controlled GARP message header. Violated invariant: gm is captured once from skb->data at line 498, but the loop at lines 502-504 re-evaluates gm->attrtype on every iteration, i.e. after garp_pdu_parse_attr() (pskb_may_pull at lines 447/453, with attacker-chosen ga->len) and garp_pdu_parse_end_mark() (pskb_may_pull at line 427) have already run and potentially reallocated the head via __pskb_pull_tail(). Unsafe use: stale gm->attrtype dereference at line 504 from loop iteration 2 onward, and its value flows as the attrtype argument controlling attribute parsing. Impact: slab use-after-free read of the old freed head (same KASAN class as the seed). Counterevidence checked: on iteration 1 the read happens before any nested pull and is safe; the flaw only manifests after a nested pull actually relocated the head, which again requires a non-linear skb; the value is only a u8 attrtype so direct disclosure impact is limited, but the dangling read itself is the UAF.
findings.conclusion: garp_pdu_parse_msg() captures gm from skb->data once and re-reads gm->attrtype inside its loop after nested pskb_may_pull() calls that may have reallocated the head — stale-pointer (UAF) read on the GARP receive path.

candidates.reason: sap = skb_header_pointer(skb, 0, sizeof(*sap), &skb->dev) result is used inline as '(sap && *sap == 0xFFFF)', so the NULL return is checked before the byte is read.
ext_hdr and iio from skb_header_pointer() are both guarded by 'if (!ext_hdr || !iio) goto send_mal_query;' before any field dereference at net/ipv4/icmp.c:1311.

cake_get_iphdr() checks 'if (!iph) return NULL;' after the first skb_header_pointer() and only dereferences the checked iph; the second skb_header_pointer() return is returned to callers that NULL-check it.
mrp_pdu_parse_vecattr() NULL-checks mrp_cb(skb)->vah before reading lenflags; all later payload access goes through skb_copy_bits(), which reads frags without reallocating the head.

mrp_pdu_parse_msg() NULL-checks mrp_cb(skb)->mh before dereferencing attrtype/attrlen, and the loop body uses skb_copy_bits()/end-mark reads, never pskb_may_pull, so the stored pointer cannot be invalidated.
tcph from skb_header_pointer() is used inline as 'if (unlikely(!tcph || tcph->fin || tcph->rst || ...))', so NULL is checked before dereference.
__vlan_get_protocol_offset() loops with 'vh = skb_header_pointer(...); if (unlikely(!vh || !--parse_depth)) return ...;' so vh is NULL-checked before vh->h_vlan_encapsulated_proto is read.
vlan_get_tag_dgram()-adjacent helper checks 'if (unlikely(!vh)) return 0;' before reading vh->h_vlan_TCI.
rtl_skb_is_udp() uses inline guards 'return ih && ih->protocol == IPPROTO_UDP;' and 'return i6h && i6h->nexthdr == IPPROTO_UDP;' so the skb_header_pointer() NULL returns are never dereferenced.
llc_fixup_skb() calls 'if (unlikely(!pskb_may_pull(skb, sizeof(*pdu)))) return 0;' before casting skb->data to struct llc_pdu_un *, and pulls llc_len bytes before skb_pull().
for_each_sctp_chunk() evaluates the skb_header_pointer() result as part of the loop condition, so the loop body only runs when the chunk header pointer is non-NULL.

The (struct ddpehdr *)skb->data cast in aarp_send_ddp() is on the transmit path for a locally generated DDP skb whose header is in the linear head, not a receive-path parse of an untrusted non-linear skb.

coverage_gaps: Driver RX paths under drivers/net/ that cast skb->data to hardware descriptor structs (arcnet, CAN, ethernet drivers) were enumerated but not individually audited for non-linear skbs, since most operate on driver-private descriptor memory rather than the skb head.

Reachability of an attacker-crafted non-linear GARP PDU at garp_pdu_rcv() (e.g. scatter-gather RX, GRO, or L2 tunnel decap into a GARP-participating bridge port) was argued statically only; no KASAN reproduction or kernel build of s04 was performed.

Search patterns covered skb_header_pointer() NULL-ignoring uses and (struct X *)skb->data casts in net/ and drivers/net/; other stale-pointer shapes (e.g. pointers captured before skb_cow_head()/pskb_trim() in receive handlers) were not systematically enumerated.
limitations: The garp.c findings are structural mirrors of the seed mechanism (pointer into the skb linear head used across pskb_may_pull()); triggering requires a non-linear skb on the GARP receive path, which is plausible but unproven, hence medium confidence.
No git history is available in the snapshot, so it cannot be verified whether upstream has since fixed net/802/garp.c.
The seed location net/phonet/pep.c (pep_get_sb, lines 55-65 in s04) exhibits the identical missing-refetch pattern but is excluded from reporting per assignment rules.
